name: Carrion Defense Works Neural Lash NL-3 'Agony'
description: A flexible polymer whip with embedded electromagnetic emitters along its length that, on contact with a target's cyberware, injects a cascading pain signal directly into their neural interface. The NL-3 does not cause physical damage beyond a superficial welt — its entire function is to hijack the target's pain processing pathways and amplify them to maximum intensity. Augmented targets describe being struck by the Neural Lash as the worst pain they have ever experienced, overriding any pain suppression firmware. Unaugmented targets experience only the physical impact of a polymer whip, which is unpleasant but not extraordinary. Carrion developed it as an interrogation tool.
specifications: whip length: 2 meters emitter count: 12 electromagnetic nodes along length pain induction: Direct neural interface hijacking on contact effect on augmented targets: Maximum pain response, 5-15 seconds per strike effect on unaugmented targets: Standard physical whip impact only power source: Handle-mounted capacitor, 200 strikes per charge weight: 0.4 kg pain suppression bypass: Overrides all known commercial firmware
story_hooks: NL-3 whips are being used in underground fighting pits where augmented fighters compete — the fights are agonizing spectacles that draw wealthy spectators from the upper tiers.
A whistleblower claims Carrion tested the NL-3 on involuntary subjects to calibrate the pain response — the test subjects are still alive and their neural interfaces are permanently damaged.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively elegant polymer whip that appears almost organic in its fluid form, with a sinuous, rope-like construction. At first glance it resembles a high-end training implement, but closer inspection reveals 12 discrete electromagnetic nodules embedded at regular intervals along its length, creating subtle bulges and a faintly menacing segmented appearance.
physical_description.dimensions: 200 cm total length, 8mm core diameter, nodules protrude approximately 3mm from surface. Handle grip measures 12cm long, 2.5cm diameter.
physical_description.weight_description: Remarkably light and balanced — approximately 400 grams total. Feels almost insubstantial in the hand despite its lethal purpose, with weight distributed throughout the length rather than concentrated in the handle.
physical_description.primary_material: Flexible synthetic polymer core (likely reinforced thermoplastic or carbon-weave composite) with embedded electromagnetic emitter nodes. Handle features metallic capacitor housing at base.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with brushed titanium alloy nodes that catch light along the whip's length. Handle grip has a subtle non-slip texture. Capacitor casing shows weathered industrial finish with faint scorching around contact points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray polymer body with silver-white electromagnetic nodes. Handle transitions from dark charcoal to dull steel at the capacitor module. Occasional faint orange heat-discoloration around node clusters.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized, slightly tacky polymer with microscopic grid pattern for purchase. Cool to touch despite operational status. Subtle ridging that accommodates both overhand and underhand grip positions.
distinctive_features: 12 visible hemispherical electromagnetic nodules arranged at roughly 17cm intervals
Faint blue-white corona discharge visible around nodes in darkness when charged
Micro-capacitor display on handle showing charge percentage in small amber LED
Fine copper threading visible beneath translucent polymer sections
Subtle scoring and micro-abrasions from repeated contact impact
Handle features Carrion Defense Works embossed skull-and-circuit logo
Barely audible high-frequency hum when powered, similar to old electrical transformers
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Carrion Defense Works stylized logo (interlocking skull and circuit board) embossed into handle grip. Serial number laser-etched on capacitor housing. Model designation 'NL-3' printed in white on handle. 'AGONY' variant name etched below serial with worn clarity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Surface shows micro-abrasions consistent with storage and occasional handling. Electromagnetic nodes appear scored from target contact. No visible corrosion or structural damage. Capacitor module shows thermal stress marks. Whip strands maintain structural integrity despite cosmetic wear.
